pullRequests.title: refactor(shadcn-lint): agentic linting - first pass, map --oh-* tokens into the Tailwind theme

reviews.body:
🟡 **Acceptable** — the direction is right (map tokens into `@theme`, let the linter reason about real utilities), and the ~1000 bracket→utility rewrites are mechanically sound. But the PR claims "every replacement is value-identical" and that is not true in three places, one of which is a real regression. The trap is instructive: the linter told an agent to "use a theme token" and the agent picked a token whose *name* matched without checking what it *compiles to*.

### Three Questions
1. **Real problem?** Yes — agents writing `bg-[var(--oh-border)]` because the design token isn't a utility is exactly the drift this fixes.
2. **Simpler way?** The `@theme` mapping is the simplest correct fix. No complaints on the approach.
3. **What will this break?** See below.

### Issue checklist (#17480)
- [x] `--oh-*` tokens mapped into `@theme inline`
- [x] bracket-token usages rewritten to first-class utilities
- [x] `no-arbitrary-values` at `warn`, other rules registered `off`
- [x] lint/build/test green
- [ ] "visual output unchanged" — **not true**, see Critical/Improvement below

**[CRITICAL ISSUES]**

- [src/components/features/chat/components/chat-input-field.tsx, L48 & L52], [src/components/features/onboarding/steps/say-hello-step.tsx, L110] **Regression — `text-[16px]` → `text-base` drops the font size.** In this repo `text-base` is a **color** utility, not a font-size utility: `--color-base: var(--oh-color-base)` is declared in `@theme inline`, so Tailwind emits `.text-base{color:var(--oh-color-base)}` and nothing for font-size (verified in the built CSS — `text-xs`/`text-sm`/`text-lg` emit `font-size`, `text-base` does not). `main` already relies on this: `bg-primary text-base` is used 24× as "dark text on a gold button". Net effect: the chat input and the onboarding hello input lose their explicit 16px and inherit whatever the parent has, and L48 gets `color: cool-grey-950` competing with `text-text-tertiary` (currently saved only by cascade order). This is a user-visible regression in the primary input surface.

**[IMPROVEMENT OPPORTUNITIES]**

- [src/tailwind.css, L56] **Silent visual change**: adding `--color-warning` re-binds the *pre-existing* `text-warning` / `bg-warning/10` / `border-warning/40` usages on `main` (openai-subscription-auth-card, free-models-note, model-selector) from HeroUI's amber `hsl(37 91% 55%)` to `#c9b974`. I built with `main`'s `tailwind.css` vs this branch's to confirm. This is probably *desirable* (those sites were off-system), but it contradicts "no visual changes intended" and should be stated in the PR rather than discovered by the next person who greps.
- [src/tailwind.css, L41] Same story for `--color-border`: `markdown/blockquote.tsx` used `border-border` from `tailwind.config.js`'s `border.DEFAULT: #242424`; it now resolves to cool-grey-700. Also `tailwind.config.js` still declares `border.DEFAULT` — two writers for one utility name. Either delete the legacy `border` entry from `tailwind.config.js` or note that `@theme` wins.
- [src/tailwind.css, L59] **Dead code**: `--radius-default` is added but `rounded-default` appears 0 times in `src/` and Tailwind doesn't emit it. Remove it or use it.
- [src/ui/divider.tsx, L10] (and 7 other `h-0.25` / `ml-0.25` sites) `[1px]` → `0.25` is `0.0625rem`, i.e. *not* value-identical to 1px (it only matches at 16px root). Tailwind has `h-px` / `ml-px` for exactly this, and `main` already uses `h-px` 11×. Use the idiom, not a fraction.
- [eslint.config.js, L394–L419] ~30 lines of comment that paraphrase the PR description ("TRIAL: …", "What remains under this rule are genuine one-offs…"). That narrative belongs in the PR / commit message; it will rot the moment someone flips a rule. Keep the docs link and a one-liner per `off` rule.

**[DEPENDENCIES]**

- [package.json, L134] **Supply chain**: `@shadcn/lint@0.1.0` was published **2026-09-14 (2 days ago)** and is the package's *first* release. It pulls `cn@0.2.6` (10 days old) and ~21 optional `oxc-parser` native binaries into the lockfile. It's a devDependency from the shadcn org so the risk is bounded, but per the 7-day rule this shouldn't merge before ~2026-09-21, and I'd want a human to eyeball the `oxc-parser` binary footprint.

**[TESTING GAPS]**

- The updated unit tests only assert the new class *strings*; nothing catches the `text-base` semantic swap because the tests don't compile CSS. That's fine — but the evidence section should then include a visual check of the chat input, not just lint/build/test output.

**[RISK ASSESSMENT]**
- [Overall PR] ⚠️ Risk Assessment: 🟡 MEDIUM — 381 files of mechanical class rewrites with one confirmed font-size regression on the primary input and two undisclosed color re-bindings; plus a 2-day-old new dev dependency with native binaries. No agent/benchmark behaviour touched.

**VERDICT:** ✅ **Worth merging** once the `text-base` regression is fixed and the PR is honest about the `warning`/`border` re-binding.

**KEY INSIGHT:** Mapping tokens into `@theme` changes the meaning of *every existing* class that shares the new name — the review surface is `git grep <utility>` on `main`, not just the diff.

_This review was posted by an AI agent (OpenHands)._

## Summary

Scope is correct: the change is entirely Canvas-owned (`eslint.config.js`, `src/components/...`, `src/utils/form-control-classes.ts`) and needs no SDK/automation/extensions counterpart. This is a bounded lint-adoption chore, matching the linked issue #17642's stated "initial PR at warn" plan.

## Verification performed on head `33c23f8b`

- **Rule is real and configured validly.** Installed `@shadcn/lint@0.1.0`; its `no-unknown-classes` schema takes `allow: string[]` compiled as anchored glob patterns (`compileEntries`/`matches`), so the two literal entries are exact matches, not prefixes. A near-match typo (`environment-switch-overla`) still warns — confirmed by running the committed probe.
- **Allow entries have real consumers.** `environment-switch-overlay` is styled in `src/index.css:134` (outside the Tailwind `@import` graph in `src/tailwind.css`), and `conversation-overview-diffs-git-action` targets `has-[.conversation-overview-diffs-git-action:hover]` in `conversation-overview-diffs-row.tsx`. Both comments in the config are accurate.
- **The four removals are inert.** Compiled CSS with the real Tailwind theme (via `@tailwindcss/node`) shows `ease`, `max-w-auto`, and `drag-over-content` each produce **zero** CSS delta versus the preflight baseline, while control utilities (`ease-in`, `max-w-full`, `flex`) do. `twMerge` preserves the removed tokens unchanged. Both dropdown wrappers compose `cn("relative", className)` with no competing max-width, and the transition helper keeps `transition-[transform] duration-75 motion-reduce:transition-none` plus the default timing function, so `ease` behavior is unchanged. Repository search found no CSS/JS/test consumer of any removed class.
- **Zero unknown-class warnings across the tree.** Chunked ESLint runs with the real flat config over every `src` directory returned `unknownClassWarnings=0` in all chunks, corroborating the PR's central claim (a full single-process `eslint src` run OOMs in this sandbox, so I used directory-scoped runs).
- **Focused tests pass.** `vitest run` on the five form/dropdown/helper suites: **5 files / 69 tests passed**, matching the PR.
- **CI for the exact head is green:** `test-and-build (ubuntu)` passed (Lint, Test, Build app, Build library) and `test-and-build (windows)` passed. `live-e2e` is skipped for fork PRs by design. The transient duplicate `PR Description Check` failure is superseded by the later success at 21:32:49Z; the `release ready` `startup_failure` is a `pull_request_target` workflow/config event untouched by this PR.

## Acceptance criteria (#17642)

- [x] Rule runs through `npm run lint` against the real theme without theme-loading/fallback warnings.
- [x] Baseline/final rule-specific findings and exception reasons recorded (`.pr/lint-verification.md`, six-to-zero inventory).
- [x] Reproducible detection/acceptance check (both committed probes pass here).
- [x] Class changes justified by emitted CSS + before/after real-app screenshots for the affected UI.
- [x] `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:lib` pass; pre-existing arbitrary-value warnings identified separately.
- [x] Other shadcn rules retain their prior settings (only `no-unknown-classes` changed).

## Non-blocking notes

- The one full-suite failure the PR discloses (`DeleteProfileModal` success-toast intermittent) is a pre-existing flake; this change touches no runtime source, and the isolated rerun passed. Not attributable to this PR.
- The `.drag-over-content` marker is removed rather than wired to the similarly named `.drag-over-ui-content` rule; deferring that styling decision is reasonable and explicitly documented.

No material correctness, security, compatibility, or architecture findings.

✅ APPROVED

The verification now shows **zero** remaining `shadcn/no-unknown-classes` findings, so could we promote this specific rule from `warn` to `error` in this PR?

That would give us a simple zero-baseline ratchet through the existing `npm run lint` CI path: every newly introduced unknown class would fail lint, while the two intentional exact exceptions remain allowed. It also avoids adding a custom warning-count script or conflating this rule with the existing `no-arbitrary-values` warning backlog.

The issue originally proposed `warn` for an incremental rollout, but since all six findings have been resolved there is no remaining debt to roll down incrementally.

_This review was posted by an AI agent (OpenHands)._

## Summary

Scoped fix in the independent verification skill: `availableMemoryBytes()` now reads `process.availableMemory()` on Darwin before the `/proc/meminfo` / `os.freemem()` fallback. The default 2,000 MiB guard, the `--min-free-mb` override, and the Linux/non-Linux paths are untouched.

## Scope

Only three files change, all under `.agents/skills/verify-openhands/` (`SKILL.md`, `control-openhands.mjs`, `control-openhands.test.mjs`). That matches the verify-skill isolation rule in `AGENTS.md` (a verify-skill PR may contain only verify-skill paths, `AGENTS.md`, and root `.pr/` evidence). No product source, backend contract, dependency, or feature-map change. Change belongs in this repository.

## Verification performed on the head

- Confirmed head `743f204fd4c845a93d11fff3f8b973c65ecd6ade`; all 15 non-skipped GitHub checks on that commit are `success` (`test-and-build (ubuntu)` and `(windows)`, `Verify skill isolation`, `Validate PR description`).
- Ran the focused suite in the workspace: `npx vitest run .agents/skills/verify-openhands` -> 2 files, 99 passed, 1 skipped.
- Confirmed the base function (`HEAD~1`) had no Darwin branch, so `os.freemem()` (unused pages only) drove the guard; the reported undercount is real.
- Verified upstream semantics: libuv 1.52 `uv_get_available_memory` on darwin returns `free_count + inactive_count + purgeable_count`, while `uv_get_free_memory` returns only `free_count`; libuv 1.51 returned `uv_get_free_memory()`. This supports the SKILL.md claim about libuv >= 1.52 and the conservative older-runtime note.
- Confirmed the direct `process.availableMemory()` call is safe at the launcher's supported floor: `cmdLaunch` enforces `nodeMajor() >= 24` before `availableMemoryBytes()` runs, and `process.availableMemory` is a writable/configurable own property of `process` on Node 24 (checked live).
- Confirmed `availableMemoryBytes()` has exactly one caller (the `launch` preflight), so the new branch cannot change unrelated paths.
- Confirmed no tracked files were modified during review.

## Acceptance criteria (issue #18644)

- [x] macOS with native available above 2,000 MiB while unused is below proceeds: Darwin case `freeMb: 300, availableMb: 8192` reaches the next prerequisite instead of exiting on memory.
- [x] Available below threshold still exits 3 before services start: `availableMb: 1024` and `availableMb: 0` cases.
- [x] `--min-free-mb` compared against available memory: `availableMb: 3000, --min-free-mb 4000` refused.
- [x] Linux `MemAvailable` and the fallback preserved: both Linux cases (with and without `/proc/meminfo`) covered.
- [x] Other platforms keep the `os.freemem()` fallback: `win32` case covered.
- [x] Change stays within `.agents/skills/verify-openhands/`.
- [x] `SKILL.md` memory wording matches the new behavior.

The new tests drive the real CLI entrypoint and preload only OS/FS memory inputs; the empty-`PATH` child stops at the missing `uvx` prerequisite, so they exercise the guard rather than a mock of it. No behavioral regression found in the changed branch or its side effects.

No material correctness, security, compatibility, or architecture findings.

✅ APPROVED
